title: The World Largest Desert Is Made of Ice
description: Discover why the coldest continent on Earth is actually its driest desert. Learn how extreme temperatures lock away moisture to create a barren polar wilderness.
instagram_caption: Antarctica is famous for its ice, but it is actually the driest desert on Earth. Follow Wonders of the Nature for more natural mysteries.

segments.narration: This freezing wind looks like snow, but is actually bone dry.
Deserts are defined by how much water they lose each year.
Here, freezing temperatures lock away water, keeping the air dry.
Cold air cannot hold moisture, preventing clouds from forming.
broll_queries: clear blue sky glacier close up

segments.narration: Without clouds, some areas have seen no rain for millions of years.
Fierce winds sweep the valleys, evaporating any tiny trace of moisture.
broll_queries: dust blowing over landscape wide shot

segments.narration: The soil here is so dry that it resembles Mars.
This makes this polar wilderness the largest desert on Earth.
It is a silent place defined by ice instead of sand.
